# Story 15.2: Launch the packaged server with an explicit non-dev NODE_ENV and verify dev-only features don't break

Status: ready-for-dev

## Story

As a developer,
I want `apps/electron/src/main.ts` to launch the packaged server child with an explicit non-dev `NODE_ENV`,
So that auth/CSRF are enforced in shipped builds while dev-only features keep working under genuine development (P0 item #2 from Aspect 9 of the critical review).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Story 15.1's red-phase tests pass: the packaged launch path sets an explicit non-dev `NODE_ENV` (`production` or a dedicated `'desktop'`) on the forked server child instead of defaulting to `'development'`.
2. Under that non-dev `NODE_ENV`, `auth.ts`'s `isDevEnvironment()` returns false and `shouldSkipAuth` does NOT skip JWT validation for all routes — auth/CSRF enforcement is active in the shipped build.
3. Genuine development/test runs keep their dev behavior: when a real developer launches with an explicit dev `NODE_ENV`, dev-only features (e.g., relaxed auth, debug endpoints) still work as before.
4. The previously-skipped tests from Story 15.1 are unskipped (`.skip()` removed) and pass; the full relevant suite is green with no pre-existing test modified, weakened, or removed.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [ ] Task 1 (AC: #1–#3): Remove skip markers and confirm red.
  - [ ] 1.1 In the specs added by Story 15.1, remove every `it.skip` marker and run the relevant test target(s), confirming the new assertions FAIL against current code (red).
- [ ] Task 2 (AC: #1): Set an explicit non-dev NODE_ENV on the packaged launch path.
  - [ ] 2.1 In `apps/electron/src/main.ts`, change the default at lines 107–108 so that when no `NODE_ENV` is present in the child env, it is set to an explicit non-dev value (`production` or a dedicated `'desktop'`) rather than `'development'`.
- [ ] Task 3 (AC: #2): Confirm auth/CSRF enforcement under non-dev.
  - [ ] 3.1 Verify `apps/server/src/app/plugins/auth.ts`'s `isDevEnvironment()` returns false and `shouldSkipAuth` does not skip JWT validation for all routes when the child runs with the new non-dev `NODE_ENV`.
- [ ] Task 4 (AC: #3): Preserve genuine dev behavior.
  - [ ] 4.1 Confirm that a real developer launch with an explicit dev `NODE_ENV` still gets dev-only features; do not break the dev path by over-broadening the non-dev default.
- [ ] Task 5 (AC: #4): Confirm green suite.
  - [ ] 5.1 Run the relevant test target(s) and confirm fully green with Story 15.1's tests now passing (unskipped).

## Dev Notes

- **Why:** `apps/electron/src/main.ts:107-108` defaults the forked server child's `NODE_ENV` to `'development'`, and `auth.ts`'s `isDevEnvironment()` (dev/test/local) makes `shouldSkipAuth` skip JWT validation for ALL routes in that mode — so the shipped desktop app runs with zero API authentication. This is P0 item #2 from Aspect 9.
- **First task is always unskip → confirm red → implement.** The red-phase tests from Story 15.1 define the target; do not edit their assertions to make them pass, only the production code.
- **Do not break genuine dev:** the fix must distinguish "packaged launch with no NODE_ENV" (→ non-dev) from "developer explicitly set a dev NODE_ENV" (→ keep dev behavior). A dedicated `'desktop'` value may be cleaner than reusing `production`.
- Vitest is the workspace test framework; server tests run via `nx test server`.

### Project Structure Notes

- Modify: `apps/electron/src/main.ts` (lines 107–108 — non-dev default for packaged launch).
- Possibly modify: `apps/server/src/app/plugins/auth.ts` (only if the new `'desktop'` value needs to be excluded from `isDevEnvironment()`'s dev set).
- Modify: Story 15.1's specs (remove `.skip()` markers only — no assertion changes).
